title: Ancient Trees in Canada: 3 Cities to Explore
meta_description: Montreal and Quebec City nurse survivors of the blight that killed 22,000 elms; Toronto's Kew Gardens oak became its first official city tree in 2022.
intro: Canada's mapped trees keep circling one epidemic. Dutch elm disease killed roughly 22,000 of Montreal's American elms, and the Last Elm of Mont-Royal is one of the few left, a self-seeded survivor growing away from the streets where the disease moved fastest. Quebec City's Plains of Abraham lost most of its mature elms the same way and still keeps about 750 of them, monitored tree by tree against the fungus a century on, alongside wych elms, a European species growing beside the American ones. Toronto took a different route: in 2022 the city named an official tree for the first time, a 220-year-old red oak in Kew Gardens with a trunk 5.3 metres round. Montreal also holds a honey locust dated from a death recorded on the gravestone beside it, and a Japanese yew that grew fifteen metres wide instead of tall.
